title: CFTC to convene Innovation Advisory Committee on August 20 for crypto, AI, and prediction markets discussion
dek: The CFTC announced plans for the inaugural meeting of its Innovation Advisory Committee on August 20, 2026, to discuss regulation of crypto assets, artificial intelligence, and prediction markets. Per the agency's press release, the meeting will be streamed live and the public may submit comments by August 27. All data points come from the CFTC announcement and have not been independently verified.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Per a CFTC press release announcement (not independently verified), Chairman Michael S. Selig is convening the Innovation Advisory Committee's first meeting on August 20 to address crypto regulation, AI, and prediction markets.
bottom_line: The CFTC's announcement of the Innovation Advisory Committee marks a formal convening of policy discussion on crypto and prediction markets at the federal level. Readers should note the agency's explicit disclaimer that advisory recommendations do not reflect Commission or government positions, and that no binding regulatory outcomes are guaranteed from the meeting. Watch for the committee membership roster, the full August 20 agenda, and any formal CFTC responses to the committee's recommendations in the months following.
body: The CFTC announced that it will hold the inaugural meeting of its Innovation Advisory Committee on Thursday, August 20, 2026, focusing discussions on the regulation of crypto assets, artificial intelligence, and prediction markets, according to a press release from the agency that has not been independently verified.

Per the agency announcement, the meeting will be streamed live on CFTC.gov. Members of the public may submit comments in connection with the meeting by August 27 through Regulations.gov or by other methods specified in the meeting notice. All comments received will be posted on Regulations.gov.

Chairman Michael S. Selig is listed as the sponsor of the Innovation Advisory Committee, according to the press release. Michael Passalacqua serves as the committee's Designated Federal Officer. The CFTC stated that the meeting agenda may change to accommodate other committee priorities.

In a statement included in the announcement, Selig said: "America has long been the global hub of financial innovation. I look forward to meeting with the entrepreneurs, thinkers, and builders of the CFTC's Innovation Advisory Committee to discuss ways emerging technologies and financial products are shaping our markets as we embark upon the new frontier of finance." This quote comes from the agency press release and reflects the announced position only.

The CFTC included a disclaimer that "the views, opinions, and information expressed by the Advisory Committees are solely those of the respective Advisory Committee and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission, its staff, or the U.S. government." This language signals that the committee's recommendations are advisory only and carry no guarantee of binding regulatory outcomes or formal rulemaking.
